deep.reconstruction:
Context: section II of a set of notes ('Litt. B'). Section I (art. 1-9) dealt with multiple-angle series. Section II takes up the summation of the 'Euler–Lagrange interpolation sum'.

Setup (art. 10). Let a_1=a, a_2=b, a_3=c, ... be m distinct indeterminates. Define
  S^n := sum_{i=1}^m a_i^n / prod_{j!=i} (a_i - a_j).
Here S^n is a label, not a power. Let
  f(x) = prod_i (x - a_i) = x^m - A x^{m-1} + B x^{m-2} - C x^{m-3} + ... ± L x ∓ M.
The upper signs hold for odd m and the lower for even m. So A=e_1, B=e_2, ..., L=e_{m-1}, M=e_m are the elementary symmetric functions, m of them, as Gauss notes.

Claim (art. 10). The S^n satisfy a linear recurrence with the coefficients of f. The reason given: every root satisfies
  a_i^n - A a_i^{n-1} + B a_i^{n-2} - ... = 0.
[My fill-in: this is a_i^{n-m} f(a_i) = 0, valid for n >= m. Divide the i-th equation by prod_{j!=i}(a_i-a_j) and add.] The result is
  S^n - A S^{n-1} + B S^{n-2} - C S^{n-3} + ... ∓ M S^{n-m} = 0  (n >= m).
The page writes this line with all '+' signs; see errors.

Theorem (art. 11). For every integer n with 0 <= n < m-1 (n=0 added in a marginal insertion), S^n = 0.

Proof (begun here, finished on the next page).
- The denominators contain m(m-1) differences a_i - a_j.
- These pair off as opposites, leaving m(m-1)/2 distinct differences for indeterminate a_i.
- Let P = prod_{i<j}(a_i - a_j), the Vandermonde product, of degree m(m-1)/2.
- Next page: put 𝔄_i = P / prod_{j!=i}(a_i - a_j). These are polynomials of degree (m-1)(m-2)/2.
- Then Q := P S^n = sum_i 𝔄_i a_i^n is a polynomial of degree (m-1)(m-2)/2 + n. Since n < m-1, this is less than m(m-1)/2.
- Q is divisible by each a_i - a_j. Hence it is divisible by P, so Q = 0 and S^n = 0. This last step is my completion of the evident plan.

Consequences (mine, not on this page). Together with S^{m-1} = 1, the corrected recurrence gives S^{m-1+k} = h_k(a_1,...,a_m), the complete homogeneous symmetric polynomial. Equivalently, S^n is the divided difference x^n[a_1,...,a_m].
errors: Sign slip in the recurrence line ('Hiedurch wird S^n + A S^{n-1} + B S^{n-2} + C S^{n-3} + D S^{n-4} + etc. = 0'). Summing the displayed root relations a^n - A a^{n-1} + B a^{n-2} - ... = 0 gives alternating signs: S^n - A S^{n-1} + B S^{n-2} - C S^{n-3} + ... = 0. The heavy ink blots before A, C, ... in the polynomial and root lines look like '+' overwritten into '-'. The same correction was evidently not made in the S-line. (Alternatively the line is right only if A, B, C, ... are the signed coefficients.)

Unstated range: the root relations a^n - A a^{n-1} + ... = 0 hold only when they are read as a^{n-m} f(a) = 0, i.e. n >= m with terms ending at ∓M a^{n-m}. For smaller n the truncated expression is not zero. The page leaves this implicit.
No error in the theorem itself. The bound n < m-1 is sharp, since S^{m-1} = 1.

results.what: sum_i a_i^n / prod_{j!=i}(a_i-a_j) = 0 for 0 <= n <= m-2, proved via the Vandermonde product and a degree/divisibility argument
results.modern_name: Euler's identity / vanishing of divided differences of low-degree monomials (Lagrange interpolation identity)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (Institutiones calculi integralis, c. 1768, and correspondence); also Lagrange; later Jacobi/Cauchy in the alternant setting

results.what: Linear recurrence for S^n with the elementary symmetric coefficients of prod(x-a_i), derived from a_i^{n-m} f(a_i) = 0
results.modern_name: Newton-type recurrence for the complete homogeneous symmetric polynomials h_k = S^{m-1+k}

results.what: Proof technique: the antisymmetric numerator P*S^n has degree below that of the Vandermonde P yet is divisible by every a_i-a_j, hence vanishes

deep.surprise_reason: These are classical identities due to Euler and Lagrange, here given a clean Vandermonde-divisibility proof. Gauss used such sums, e.g. in quadrature and interpolation work, and the editor's pencil cross-reference to Werke III p. 265 suggests related material appears in print. Nothing here would surprise a specialist.
